chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
«The one who is habitual in drinking wine, Allah (Exalted and Glorious) will meet him on the Day he meets him, like a worshipper of an idol.»
ai.seo_question: What is the status of a habitual wine drinker on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize that habitual wine consumption (*mudmin*) elevates the drinker to the spiritual rank of an idolater (*abidith-than*), not merely due to the substance but due to the constancy of the sin. This comparison underscores the concept of *tashbih* (likening) the intoxicated state to the prostration before false deities, a key theme in Shia theological discussions on the degradation of the soul. The hadith serves as a critical link between jurisprudential rulings on *khamr* and broader metaphysical consequences in the afterlife.
